title: 26th Sitting of second session of 2026
summary: The sitting opened at 09:01 and the minutes of sittings 19 to 21 were accepted. Members then put questions to the Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises, Hassan Zareer, on the size of the state payroll, dismissals and rightsizing in state companies, the dollar shortage, loan repayments and the deficit. After question time the Majlis debated Dr. Ahmed Shamheed's motion calling on the government to halt the Maldives Plus residency programme and disclose its agreements, and the debate was closed with the vote left for the day's voting time. A General Committee report on removing clause (l) of Rule 257-1 (the petition rule) was introduced and its debate had started when this part ends. The PDF text is partly garbled, so counts and gists are best-effort. This part finishes the debate on a committee report about removing a clause from Rule 257 of the Majlis rules (the petition rules), then covers the Foreign Currency Act amendment bill, where MDP and PNC members traded claims about the dollar shortage and government money printing. The Majlis voted 58-9 to extend the second session to 27 August 2026, passed the Rule 257 amendment 56-10, approved ratifying the Multinational Maritime Defence Coalition charter 58-1, and rejected an MDP resolution on the Maldives Pool Residence Programme 10-55. The Foreign Currency bill was sent back to the Finance Committee for more study. The next sitting is set for 24 August 2026 at 09:00. The text layer is partly garbled, so debate positions are summarised loosely; vote counts are clear.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: As Finance and Public Enterprises Minister, said dismissals over political affiliation are not government policy and rightsizing includes redundancy packages and an SME fund.
Said the dollar shortage largely stems from the USD 500 million sukuk repayment and that the salary bill is about MVR 1.4 billion a month.
Said one state company has been dissolved, another is in liquidation, and that some questions would be answered in writing.

speakers.name: Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Asked about money supply and dollar shortage, and whether Bank of Maldives funds count as money supply.
Moved that the Maldives Plus residency programme be halted and its agreements disclosed to the Majlis.
Argued the programme could cost the state revenue and objected to claims it was a plain investor-visa scheme.
Said MDP would not oppose the bill's main points but argued it will not end the dollar shortage without wider fixes, and criticised the lack of a crisis plan at the monetary authority.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Asked why state-company staff said to be linked to the MDP are being dismissed and on what criteria.
Asked what the Financial Reform Commissioner's office is doing, how many state companies were closed, and why recurrent spending rose despite cost-cutting claims.
Said he wrote to the National Pay Commission and got no reply, and criticised the sudden change to the petition rule.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Asked whether steps taken to cut the yearly budget deficit will give good results ahead.
On Rule 257, said petitions reach the floor once the required number of signatures is met, and that the amendment widens citizens' chance to be heard.
On the Foreign Currency bill, said the previous government printed MVR 16 billion and that this government does not print money without Majlis approval.
Moved to send the bill back to the Finance Committee, saying all resorts must convert foreign currency under the law and black-market dollar trading needs more work.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Asked about the monthly state salary bill, unpaid amounts owed to contractors and spending in October 2023.
Raised a past USD 55 million payout; the chair stopped the line because the case was decided by a court.
Argued that petitions are how citizens raise concerns, and questioned why petitions should not reach the floor for debate given the government's large majority.
Pointed to citizen petitions over land-acquisition powers in the Decentralization bill as an example of concerns the Majlis should hear.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Asked whether recent political appointees were chosen for technical needs.
Called the change to the petition rule a hasty, controversial move that weakens an electronic petition system the Majlis had created.
Alleged payments to online supporters, which the chair asked him not to say without proof.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Asked how far the political-post reduction has gone, how many were released or newly hired, and whether the criteria target one political camp.
On Rule 257, said his amendment opens more room for citizens to voice views and accused opposition members of misrepresenting it.
Presented the Finance Committee report on the Foreign Currency bill, citing rising foreign-currency deposits in banks and tourism-sector deposit growth, and asked the Majlis to pass it.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Asked when the World Bank and IMF began flagging the large salary bill.
Asked about the revenue impact of the proposed tax bill and its benefit to Maldivian travel agents.
Seconded Ibrahim Falah's motion to send the Foreign Currency bill back to the Finance Committee.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Asked when the Abu Dhabi Fund-backed hospital in Velidhoo will move ahead.
Said the Noonu Atoll resort development project is real, protects the reef and benefits local people, and called opposing claims untrue.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Asked what benefit the economy gets from repaying long-standing loans.
Asked how much SME loan money was issued, the monthly salary cost and the monthly cost of running state companies.

speakers.name: Mohamed Niushad
positions: Asked how many state-enterprise staff were let go and how many hired since November 2023.
Asked the minister's view on raising withholding tax to 15 percent.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Asked how much was overspent on projects run through state companies under earlier governments and whether recovery is possible.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Asked whether state-company staff doubled because work grew or for political reasons.
Asked how many state companies run without subsidy and what is being done to make them self-sufficient.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Asked when loans for people leaving state companies begin and how funds will be used.
Asked why waived tourism taxes were not offered to small businesses.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Asked whether the large loan repayments were deferred for political reasons.
As General Committee rapporteur, presented the report on removing clause (l) of Rule 257-1.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Asked whether a plan to cut political posts is under way and how many political appointees there were in 2019-2023 versus now.

speakers.name: Ashraf Rasheed
positions: Asked whether projects signed before the 2023 presidential election were budgeted and signed in line with finance law.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Said about 18,000 staff were hired under the earlier government, asked why around 4,000 are being let go and whether finding revenue is the minister's duty.

speakers.name: Ahmed Zahir
positions: Asked whether pay will become standardised when the redundancy package ends, given payroll shares above the usual benchmark.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Asked what is being done about the dollar shortage, when small contractors will be paid, and how much is owed on foreign loans.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Asked how much is spent on political posts and what is behind the dollar rate problem.

speakers.name: Abdulla Shareef
positions: Asked about tsunami donation money for Fiyaludhoo and the loss from land transfers linked to HDC.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Asked whether the minister knows of dollars from state companies being sold on the black market and fuel sold to resorts at high prices.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Asked how much money has been set aside to revive small businesses damaged under the previous government.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: Raised a point of order objecting to claims about PNC paying members and activists.

speakers.name: Mohamed Dawoodh
positions: Presented the Foreign Relations Committee report: on 16 August the committee agreed unanimously among members present to recommend that the Majlis approve ratifying the maritime defence coalition charter.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aifan
positions: Raised a point of order saying members should not mislead the public with false claims and referred to the 19th Majlis; the chair did not accept it as a point of order.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Raised a point of order saying Shamheed's printing claim contradicted the facts and that the government has not printed money; the chair accepted it and asked Shamheed to speak accordingly.

decisions: Chair declared the minutes of sittings 19 to 21 of 2026 accepted as no amendments were submitted.
Question time to the Finance and Public Enterprises Minister was closed at the time limit.
Debate on the motion to halt the Maldives Plus residency programme was closed; the motion goes to a vote at the day's voting time.
Chair accepted the point of order raised by the member for Velidhoo and declined to treat the one from the member for Vilimale' as a point of order.
Sitting broke for recesses 10:32 to 12:03 and 12:03 to 13:01; the session was noted as extended to 20 August 2026.
The second session of the Majlis was extended to 27 August 2026 (58-9).
The amendment to Rule 257 removing sub-clause (ޅ), as reviewed by the General Committee, was passed (56-10).
The Majlis approved ratifying the Charter of the Multinational Maritime Defence Coalition (58-1, 6 abstentions).
The MDP resolution on the Maldives Pool Residence Programme was rejected (10-55).
The Foreign Currency Act amendment bill was sent back to the Finance Committee for further study (58-0, 2 abstentions).
The next sitting was set for Monday 24 August 2026 at 09:00.
